questions.q: When reason and emotional pressure pull in different directions, what does the editorial advise?
options: Postpone the decision until feelings settle
Not quite. The article says: Meet the rational demand, and handle the emotional pressure with tact.
Give way to family feeling first
Not quite. The article says: Meet the rational demand, and handle the emotional pressure with tact.
Follow whichever is felt more strongly
Not quite. The article says: Meet the rational demand, and handle the emotional pressure with tact.
Meet the rational demand, and handle the emotional pressure with tact
Yes. Emotions can be managed; the laws of nature cannot be altered.
questions.rationale: “Emotional pressures are always manageable but rational demands do not give man a second option.”

questions.q: A woman’s mother was angry whenever she returned late from a job she needed. What did the author suggest she say?
options: “My work is not your concern”
Not quite. The article says: “Mother, I am hungry right now. Please give me food and we shall talk later”.
“I shall leave the job tomorrow”
Not quite. The article says: “Mother, I am hungry right now. Please give me food and we shall talk later”.
Nothing at all, until the anger passed
Not quite. The article says: “Mother, I am hungry right now. Please give me food and we shall talk later”.
“Mother, I am hungry right now. Please give me food and we shall talk later”
Right. A gentle reply defused the moment and she kept her job.
questions.rationale: The author advised her to keep the job, which reason required, and to manage her mother’s anger politely – “in this way her problem was solved comfortably.”

questions.q: The earth revolves around the sun. What is this a picture of, in the article?
options: The shortness of human life
Not quite. The article says: A life centred on God – which man must choose of his own free will.
The dependence of the weak on the strong
Not quite. The article says: A life centred on God – which man must choose of his own free will.
A life centred on God – which man must choose of his own free will
Yes. The earth is compelled; man surrenders by choice.
The sameness of every year
Not quite. The article says: A life centred on God – which man must choose of his own free will.
questions.rationale: “Man must indeed revolve around God, just as the earth revolves around the sun… man, of his own free will, should surrender to God.”

questions.q: What, according to the article, happens to a person who does not find God?
options: He turns naturally to science
Not quite. The article says: The urge remains, so he gives the place of God to some created thing.
The urge to worship fades away
Not quite. The article says: The urge remains, so he gives the place of God to some created thing.
He becomes free of all dependence
Not quite. The article says: The urge remains, so he gives the place of God to some created thing.
The urge remains, so he gives the place of God to some created thing
Well read. A person, a force of nature, an idea, or the self.
questions.rationale: “It is possible for man not to accept the real God as God, but it is not possible for anyone to save himself or herself from granting the status of divinity to something other than God.”

questions.q: The Prophet declined an offer to turn a valley of Makkah into gold, preferring to be fed one day and hungry the next. Why?
options: Because wealth is forbidden to prophets
Not quite. The article says: So that in hunger he might call on God, and when satisfied thank and praise Him.
So that in hunger he might call on God, and when satisfied thank and praise Him
Exactly. Each condition calls forth its own feeling of faith.
Because hunger is good for health
Not quite. The article says: So that in hunger he might call on God, and when satisfied thank and praise Him.
Because gold was of no use in Makkah
Not quite. The article says: So that in hunger he might call on God, and when satisfied thank and praise Him.
questions.rationale: “So that when I feel hungry, I can beseech You and remember You and when I am full and satiated, I can praise You and thank You.”

questions.q: The article traces a chain of killings among the sultans of Granada after 1302. What point does this history illustrate?
options: Once the sanctity of life is broken, one murder opens the door to many
Yes. This is why killing one person is likened to killing all mankind.
Kingdoms fall when rulers are too gentle
Not quite. The article says: Once the sanctity of life is broken, one murder opens the door to many.
Royal families should be kept small
Not quite. The article says: Once the sanctity of life is broken, one murder opens the door to many.
Spain was badly governed for centuries
Not quite. The article says: Once the sanctity of life is broken, one murder opens the door to many.
questions.rationale: “A person who commits such a crime gives licence to others in society… The murder of one human being opens the door to the killing of mankind.”

questions.q: Countless stars move at great speed without colliding. What does the article say this teaches about living in society?
options: Speed and energy matter most
Not quite. The article says: Each person must keep within the sphere God has set, and peace follows.
The strong should lead and the rest follow
Not quite. The article says: Each person must keep within the sphere God has set, and peace follows.
People should have as little to do with each other as possible
Not quite. The article says: Each person must keep within the sphere God has set, and peace follows.
Each person must keep within the sphere God has set, and peace follows
Right. Crossing limits brings clashes.
questions.rationale: “If everyone moves in his respective sphere, a state of peace is automatically established in society. But when people cross their limits… society will witness clashes and confrontations.”

questions.q: What does the article say fasting symbolises beyond a month of going hungry?
options: A lifelong culture of dedication – simple living and high thinking, free of distraction
Yes. The believer is “a man of mission.”
A yearly test of physical endurance
Not quite. The article says: A lifelong culture of dedication – simple living and high thinking, free of distraction.
A way to save on food
Not quite. The article says: A lifelong culture of dedication – simple living and high thinking, free of distraction.
A custom kept for the sake of community
Not quite. The article says: A lifelong culture of dedication – simple living and high thinking, free of distraction.
questions.rationale: “It symbolizes a lifelong culture, that is, a culture of dedication… the adoption of the well-known formula — simple living, high thinking.”

questions.q: How, according to the article, does Satan lead people into wrongdoing?
options: By removing their free will
Not quite. The article says: By making evil look attractive – dressing false arguments as sound ones.
By physically compelling them
Not quite. The article says: By making evil look attractive – dressing false arguments as sound ones.
By making evil look attractive – dressing false arguments as sound ones
Correct. He works on the mind, not by force.
By hiding the truth from prophets
Not quite. The article says: By making evil look attractive – dressing false arguments as sound ones.
questions.rationale: “He does it by allurement… It is to present a baseless argument as a strong argument in favour of an action… They find constructive words for their destructive activities.”

questions.q: What does the article compare to the forbidden tree, and what does it see as the sign that the limit has been crossed?
options: Large families; overcrowding
Not quite. The article says: A life of luxury beyond real need; global warming.
A life of luxury beyond real need; global warming
Well reasoned. The earth’s resources allow need, not greed.
Scientific curiosity; space travel
Not quite. The article says: A life of luxury beyond real need; global warming.
City life; the loss of villages
Not quite. The article says: A life of luxury beyond real need; global warming.
questions.rationale: “A life of luxury was, for man, like the forbidden tree of Paradise… Global warming is like a proclamation by nature that this target of man is never going to be fulfilled in this present world.”
